newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 10.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Association of Southeast Asian Nations may postpone its admission of Cambodia until December in light of the violent coup that raised serious doubts about the country's readiness to become a member with Laos and Burma later this month. ASEAN foreign ministers will hold an emergency meeting today in Kuala Lumpur to discuss the situation and decide how the grouping will react. (THE NATION)

- Plans to upgrade the Police Department into a bureau under the direct control of the interior minister have come under strong criticism. The envisioned National Police Bureau could become a mafia organisation if controlled by a bad politician, says Democrat leader Chuan Leekpai. (BANGKOK POST)

- Non-drafting members of the Constitution Drafting Assembly (CDA) have flexed their collective muscle to deal another humiliating blow to the academic-dominated vetting panel, further undoing the panel's work on the draft charter. The vetting panel has suffered defeats for three consecutive days, seeing its version of the charter changed article by article since the CDA began its second reading of the draft on Monday. (THE NATION)

- Civil servants who give their bosses gifts on special occasions with values beyond set limits will be accused of bribery and subject to disciplinary action. Education Minister Sukhavich Rangsitphol says the National Culture Commission has proposed the plan after the office failed to persuade government officials to reduce spending by sending only cards on special occasions. (THE NATION)

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh was tight-lipped over a report that Thailand was seeking up to $20 billion in loans to bolster reserves and restore investor confidence, while his cabinet members gave conflicting signals. If the loans are secured it would be the biggest international bailout package since the 1994 peso devaluation, when the United States and the International Monetary Fund lent Mexico $50 billion. (THE NATION)

- The Bank of Thailand (BOT) says that select commercial banks and finance sector companies will be allowed to meet the new bad loan provision requirements over five years as against the earlier two years. In the midst of an economic downturn, the relaxation of the timeframe is seen as giving these financial institutions some breathing space. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Foreign banks have cut their credit lines to all Thai financial institutions, except major commercial banks, to avoid risks. They say they will resume lending to Thai companies when uncertainties plaguing the country's financial sector have been cleared. (BANGKOK POST)
